Last Thursday (Nov 12), a config change in ingest v2.14.0 raised the default batch size from 1 MB to 10 MB, which pushed ingest-worker pods past their 512 Mi memory limit on the first large batch. They crash-looped, and because the change rolled out to all pods at once, every workspace saw stale dashboards for 3h40 (08:47–12:27 UTC). There was no consumer-lag alert, so detection came via a Sentry out-of-memory alert 27 minutes after deploy [1].

No customer data was lost: events kept landing in Kafka and were just processed late. Lior's Nov 13 reconciliation confirmed event counts per workspace match the Kafka offsets for the incident window [1][4].

Fixes and prevention:
- Rollback to v2.13.3 resolved it; ingest#419 reverted the default and added a memory guard (merged Nov 13) [1].
- KES-431: page on-call when consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes (Noa, due Nov 20) [1].
- KES-432: ingest config changes go to a canary pool first instead of all pods (Daniel, due Nov 27) [1].
- KES-433: raise worker memory to 1 Gi and add a batch-size load test (Lior, due Nov 27) [1].

Four customers contacted support; Orbitly is also asking for an SLA service credit under its MSA, which Sam is reviewing with finance [3].
